tip: A neural network design from 2017 that uses attention to relate every part of an input to every other part, powering modern language models.
Long short-term memory, a recurrent neural network that processes sequences step by step while keeping a memory of earlier inputs.
Convolutional neural network, a model that scans images with small learned filters to pick out edges, textures and larger shapes.
A generative model that learns to turn random noise into realistic images or other data by reversing a gradual noising process.
An open-source text-to-image diffusion model released in 2022 that generates pictures from written prompts on a single consumer GPU.
A model that learns to translate images between two styles, such as healthy and diseased scans, without needing matched pairs of examples.
Neural radiance field, a method that learns a 3D scene from ordinary photos so new viewpoints can be rendered photorealistically.
Large language model, an AI system trained on vast amounts of text to understand and generate human-like writing and code.
An AI model that takes both images and text as input, so it can describe pictures, answer questions about them or read charts.
One of the most capable AI models available at a given time, typically a very large system built by a major AI lab.
Low-rank adaptation: fine-tuning a large model by training small add-on matrices instead of all its weights; PEFT is the library implementing it.
Continuing to train an already trained model on a smaller, task-specific dataset so it adapts to a new job.
Storing a model's numbers with fewer bits, such as 8-bit integers instead of 32-bit decimals, to make it smaller and faster.
Running most calculations in 16-bit floating point (FP16) and only sensitive steps in 32-bit, which cuts memory use and speeds up GPUs.
Training a student model to match the outputs of a teacher model; in self-distillation the same network plays both roles.
A prompting technique in which a language model writes out intermediate reasoning steps before giving its final answer.
Reasoning carried out inside a model as continuous hidden vectors rather than as written words, so the steps are not directly readable.
A 2025 method that compresses a model's written reasoning into continuous hidden states by having the model teach itself (self-distillation).
Chain of continuous thought, a 2024 Meta method that lets a language model reason by feeding its hidden states back into itself.
Supervised implicit chain-of-thought, a 2025 training add-on that supervises each hidden reasoning step to make latent reasoning more stable.
A research field that reverse-engineers what is happening inside a neural network to explain how it produces its outputs.
The mathematics of how a state changes over time under fixed rules, used here to study how reasoning evolves step by step.
A region that a changing system settles into over time; nearby trajectories are pulled toward it and stay there.
A technique that breaks a sequence of measurements into patterns that each grow, shrink or oscillate at a fixed rate over time.
A visualization method that maps high-dimensional data into two or three dimensions while preserving both local clusters and gradual transitions.
UMAP, t-SNE and PCA are methods that squeeze data with hundreds of dimensions down to two or three so it can be plotted.
A diagnostic technique that trains a small classifier on a model's internal activations to test what information those activations encode.
An experiment that removes or swaps one component of a system at a time to measure how much that component contributes.
A list of numbers that represents an item such as a word, image or data point so that similar items end up close together.
A mechanism that lets a neural network weigh which parts of its input matter most when it produces each piece of output.
The stage where a trained model is run on new inputs to produce predictions, as opposed to the training stage.
Retrieval-augmented generation: the model first looks up relevant documents and then writes its answer using them, which reduces made-up facts.
An open-source toolkit that scores retrieval-augmented systems on measures such as faithfulness and context recall without needing human-written labels.
An open-source framework for building multi-step AI agents as a graph of nodes, with state that persists between steps.
A system design in which several specialized AI programs each handle one part of a task and hand results to one another.
When an AI model states something false or invented as if it were fact, often fluently and with apparent confidence.
A workflow in which a person reviews or approves an AI system's decisions, especially the high-risk ones, before they take effect.
How well a model's stated confidence matches reality; a calibrated model that says 80% confident is right about 80% of the time.
A classic text scoring method that weights a word by how often it appears in one document relative to how common it is overall.
A score from -1 to 1 for how closely two lists of numbers point in the same direction, used to compare documents or embeddings.
Latent Dirichlet allocation, a statistical method that discovers the topics running through a collection of documents from the words they share.
A procedural generation algorithm that fills a grid tile by tile, always choosing tiles that fit their neighbors under given adjacency rules.
Recovering a 3D model of a scene and the camera positions from a set of ordinary overlapping 2D photographs.
The pixel distance between where a reconstructed 3D point lands when projected back into a photo and where it was actually observed.
Estimating how a camera has moved through space by combining its video frames with readings from a motion sensor (IMU).
The apparent motion of each pixel between two consecutive video frames, used to track how objects and the camera are moving.
Labeling every pixel of an image by what it belongs to, such as tumor versus healthy tissue or road versus car.
NVIDIA's software that rewrites a trained model into a form that runs as fast as possible on its GPUs, often several times faster.
Open Neural Network Exchange, a common file format for trained models so one built in PyTorch can run in other tools.
A way to save a PyTorch model as a self-contained program that can run without Python, typically as the first step toward deployment.
NVIDIA's platform for writing programs that run on its graphics processors, which is how most deep learning gets its speed.
The response time that 95 out of 100 requests finish within; it captures how slow the worst typical cases are, not the average.
A tool that packages an application with everything it needs into a container, so it runs the same on any machine or cloud.
An open-source system that runs and manages many containers across a cluster of machines, restarting and scaling them automatically.
Continuous integration and delivery: automatically building, testing and releasing software every time code changes, instead of doing it by hand.
The practice of deploying, monitoring and maintaining machine learning models in production, borrowing automation habits from software operations.
Open-source monitoring tools: Prometheus collects time-stamped metrics from running services and Grafana turns them into live dashboards.
A tool that creates and updates cloud infrastructure from configuration files, so servers and networks are defined in code rather than clicked together.
An Amazon cloud service that reads text, tables and form fields out of scanned documents and PDFs automatically.
Amazon's cloud service for calling large language models from several providers through one interface, without managing any model servers.
Amazon's service for running small pieces of code on demand, billed per execution, with no server to set up or maintain.
Robot Operating System 2, an open-source framework in which robot software is built as separate programs that exchange messages.
Google's open-source toolkit for real-time perception tasks such as tracking hands, faces and body poses from a live camera.
The most widely used open-source library of image and video processing functions, from reading frames to detecting shapes.
The scripting interface of Blender, a free 3D modeling program, which lets code build, animate and render scenes automatically.
A browser technology that draws hardware-accelerated 2D and 3D graphics directly on a web page without any plugin.
An open-source Python library for wrapping a machine learning model in a simple web interface that anyone can try in a browser.
A model from OpenAI that maps images and text into the same numerical space, so it can judge how well a caption fits a picture.
A score for how closely a generated image matches its text prompt, computed by comparing the two with the CLIP model.
Fréchet inception distance, a score for how close generated images are to real ones in statistical terms; lower is better.
Two image quality scores against a reference picture: PSNR measures raw pixel error and SSIM measures perceived structural similarity.
Absolute trajectory error is the overall gap between an estimated path and the true path; relative pose error measures drift over short segments.
The 2020 edition of the Brain Tumor Segmentation challenge, a public set of labeled MRI scans used to benchmark tumor detection.
Two standard test sets of math word problems, grade-school level and competition level, used to measure how well language models reason.
The International Conference on Machine Learning, one of the three most selective annual research conferences in the field.
A conference format in which accepted research is presented on a large printed sheet and discussed with attendees one on one.
A 2026 research venue; the FairPrep paper was submitted to its regular paper track, the track for complete full-length studies.
Graduate Qualifying Project, the capstone of WPI's data science master's degree, in which a student team solves a problem for an outside sponsor.
A part-time paid university position in which a graduate student supports a professor's research or teaching alongside their own degree.
Optional Practical Training lets F-1 student visa holders work in the US for 12 months after graduating, plus 24 more months for STEM degrees.
